career_ladder.note: The International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) is the unified statutory regulator established under the International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019, governing offshore financial centers in India (GIFT City, Gandhinagar). Officers recruited as Assistant Managers (Grade 'A') serve as the core regulatory workforce overseeing offshore banking, international capital markets, global fintech entities, bullion exchange, and international reinsurance. Officers progress through executive regulatory grades based on merit, annual performance appraisals, and regulatory board selection.

exam_scheme.note: Selection to IFSCA Grade 'A' (Assistant Manager) is conducted through a three-stage competitive process: Phase I (Online Screening Examination consisting of two papers), Phase II (Online Examination consisting of two papers with 1/3rd and 2/3rd aggregate weightage), and Phase III (Personal Interview). Negative marking of 1/4th (0.25 marks) is deducted for each incorrect answer across objective papers in Phase I and Phase II.

stages.stage_name: Phase I: Online Screening Examination (2 Papers, 100 Marks Each)
stages.source_label: IFSCA — Scheme of Phase I Online Examination (Notification 2024)

papers.paper_name: Paper 1 (All Streams): General Awareness (incl. financial sector), English Language, Quantitative Aptitude, Test of Reasoning

Paper 2 (General Stream): Financial Sector General Awareness, Economic & Social Development, Indian Economy, Global Economy, IFSCA Act, Union Budget, Economic Survey, Banking, Capital Market, Insurance, Pensions, Bullion
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum cut-off 40% (Aggregate cut-off for Phase I: 40%)

stages.stage_name: Phase II: Online Examination (2 Papers, 100 Marks Each)
stages.source_label: IFSCA — Scheme of Phase II Online Examination (Notification 2024)

papers.paper_name: Paper 1: English (Descriptive Test — Precis Writing, Essay Writing, Business Comprehension)
papers.negative_marking: Descriptive writing test (1/3rd weightage towards Phase II merit)

papers.paper_name: Paper 2 (General Stream): IFSCA Act, GIFT IFSC Regulations, Central Government Schemes in Financial Sector, Global Financial Centers, Banking, Securities, Insurance, Foreign Exchange, FinTech
papers.negative_marking: -0.25 marks for each wrong answer (2/3rd weightage towards Phase II merit)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum cut-off 40% (Aggregate cut-off for Phase II: 40%)

stages.source_label: IFSCA — Phase III Interview Scheme and Final Merit Calculation

papers.negative_marking: Comprehensive personal interview evaluating regulatory aptitude and financial domain competence
papers.qualifying_threshold: Final merit computed with 85% weightage for Phase II and 15% weightage for Interview

financial_package.estimate_note: Officers in Grade A receive a starting basic pay of ₹44,500/month. Total monthly gross emoluments are approximately ₹1,43,000/month without official accommodation (or ₹1,12,000/month if availing leased accommodation). Allowances include Dearness Allowance, Grade Allowance, Special Allowance, Local Compensatory Allowance (GIFT City/Gandhinagar), Family Allowance, and Learning Allowance.
official_perks: Authority leased residential accommodation or substantial House Rent Allowance in GIFT City / Gandhinagar / Ahmedabad
Conveyance allowance / official vehicle fuel reimbursement per regulatory norms
Comprehensive medical facilities with cashless hospitalization for officer and dependent family members
Subsidized residential lease, book grant, newspaper reimbursement, and residential office equipment allowance
Leave Travel Concession (LTC) / Foreign travel study provisions per Authority rules
Defined contribution benefits under New Pension Scheme (NPS) and Authority gratuity scheme

competition_benchmarks.note: IFSCA Grade A is a highly selective regulatory competition attracting chartered accountants, corporate lawyers, master's degree holders in economics/finance, and MBAs targeting GIFT City financial regulation.

years.selectivity_ratio: approx. 1 in 1850 overall selectivity (10 notified vacancies in General stream; ~450 shortlisted for Phase II and ~35 called for Interview)
